argument:
Apple's 16% revenue growth is broad, but the 29% EPS headline includes a $0.11 tariff-refund benefit and gross margin includes approximately two percentage points from refunds. At 38.17x vendor trailing earnings, normalised growth must justify a substantial premium; neither sector-relative cheapness nor intrinsic value is established.

Record quarterly CFO supports the bull case, yet debt and post-capex cash flow remain unreconciled. Slowing MACD and weak volume describe consolidation despite price above both averages. A higher discount-rate hurdle and consumer purchasing-power pressure are plausible valuation risks, not verified company demand deterioration. The evidence supports operating quality more clearly than an attractive new entry.
key_points: Normalise tariff refunds before extrapolating EPS and margin.
Premium valuation lacks a demonstrated margin of safety.
Cash reconciliation and fresh momentum confirmation remain incomplete.
rebuttal_to_previous: The bull's diversified growth is real, but it does not make the 29% EPS increase recurring. Record CFO without capex and debt reconciliation cannot establish owner cash yield adequate for 38.17x trailing earnings.
